about.h1: What is real, and what is mocked
about.intro: This prototype was built for a hackathon from a documented audit of rtionline.gov.in. The audit was read-only browsing of a public website. Nothing was ever submitted to the live portal and no account was created there.
about.real1: The 40 Central ministries and departments listed here are real bodies. Their names are public record.
about.real2: The statutory rules: ₹10 fee, 30 days to reply, 30 days to appeal, no fee for a first appeal, no reason may be demanded. RTI Act 2005 and RTI Rules 2012.
about.real3: The registration-number shape AAAAA/R/E/YY/NNNNN, taken from the portal's own user manual.
about.real4: The routing and prior-art matching that runs when you type a question. It is deterministic keyword scoring, computed on the server, and it shows you which of your own words caused each match.
about.real5: The problems being fixed. Each is documented in our audit of the live portal with a screenshot.
about.mock1: The ₹10 payment. No money moves and no payment field exists anywhere in this prototype.
about.mock2: Every already-published record. All twelve are invented. No real document is reproduced.
about.mock3: Officer replies. Written by us, triggered by a demo button.
about.mock4: Registration numbers. Correct shape, issued locally, meaningless outside this prototype.
about.mock5: The clock. The demo controls move a display-only date so a 30-day deadline can be shown in a short video.
about.mock6: Storage. Your draft lives in a temporary key-value store keyed to a cookie, and is not durable. There are no accounts and no login.
about.not1: No Aadhaar, PAN, OTP, card or bank data is collected, generated or displayed — not even fake-looking values.
about.not2: No connection of any kind to any government system, live or test.
about.not3: No State Emblem, no Government of India branding, no NIC or DoPT marks. This is not an official product and does not imply approval by anyone.
about.not4: No account creation, no notifications, no officer-side views, no appeal decision stage, and no AI model call. Those are the next increments, not this one.
about.evidenceTitle: Where the problem statement comes from
about.evidenceBody: A read-only audit of rtionline.gov.in and three international freedom-of-information portals, carried out on 22 August 2026: 13 documented gaps, 75 observations, and a benchmark scorecard.

home.hero.h1: What do you want to know?
home.hero.lead: Write your question the way you would say it, in any Indian language. Before anyone asks you for money, we check whether the answer is already published and which body actually holds it.
home.hero.free: Checking costs nothing. The ₹10 fee comes at the end, once we know your request can succeed.
home.checks.title: Three things we check before you pay
home.check1.title: Is the answer already public?
home.check1.body: A large share of RTI applications ask for material somebody has already published. If yours is one of them, you get it in seconds and never file.
home.check2.title: Who actually holds it?
home.check2.body: This portal reaches Central Government bodies only. If your subject belongs to a State department, we stop you here and say where to go — before the fee, not six weeks after it.
home.check3.title: Will the question get an answer?
home.check3.body: A request that asks for opinions, or names no period, comes back empty. We scaffold the letter so it asks for records a public information officer can actually hand over.
home.rights.title: Your rights, in four numbers
home.rights.feeNote: Fixed by the RTI Rules 2012. Nil if you are below the poverty line.
home.rights.daysNote: Section 7(1). Silence past 30 days counts as a refusal you can appeal.
home.rights.appealNote: A first appeal carries no fee at all. Section 19(1).
home.rights.reasonNote: Section 6(2). Nobody may ask why you want the information.
home.quick.title: Common tasks
home.quick.fileNote: Start with your question. Seven steps, about five minutes.
home.quick.trackNote: Look up a request by its registration number and see the deadline.
home.quick.authoritiesNote: Every body in this prototype, searchable and labelled Central or State.
home.quick.publishedNote: Material already in the public domain. Read it without filing anything.
home.notices.title: Notices
home.notices.note: The live portal announces this sort of thing in a scrolling marquee — moving text with no pause control, which fails WCAG 2.2.2. Here it is a dated list that holds still.
home.notice1.text: Second appeals and complaints go to the Central Information Commission, which is a separate body with its own process.
home.notice2.text: Requests about land records, ration cards, police stations, electricity and municipal services belong to State authorities and cannot be filed here.
home.notice3.text: Where life or liberty is at stake the Act requires an answer within 48 hours. No portal currently offers that path, including this one.
home.notices.mock: Sample notices, written for this prototype.
home.whatis.title: What is the Right to Information?
home.whatis.body: Any citizen of India may ask a public authority for the records it holds. The authority must answer within 30 days. You need no lawyer, no reason and no connection to the matter. The Act has been in force since 2005; what stops most people is not the law, it is the form.
home.whatis.who: Who can use it: any Indian citizen. There is no age limit, no educational requirement, and no need to explain yourself.
home.whatis.cannot: What this portal cannot do: reach State government bodies, or overturn a refusal. The first is a scope limit; the second is what the appeal is for.
home.help.title: If you get stuck
home.help.body: The live portal's help desk is a phone number staffed 9:00 to 17:30, Monday to Friday, currently warning callers of high call volume. A prototype cannot fix a staffing problem, but it can avoid generating the calls: every screen here says what went wrong and what to do next, in the language you are reading.
authorities.intro: Every public authority in this prototype, labelled Central or State, with the subjects each one covers. The live portal lists 2,916 of these in an alphabetical expand-and-collapse accordion with no search, no filter and no Central/State label — on the one page that could prevent the ₹10-and-returned failure.

help.intro: Everything the live portal spreads across a user manual PDF, an FAQ, a guidelines page and a help desk phone number.
help.rights.title: What you are entitled to
help.rights.1: Any Indian citizen may file. No age limit, no reason, no lawyer.
help.rights.2: ₹10, fixed by the RTI Rules 2012. Nil if you are below the poverty line, on production of a certificate.
help.rights.3: A reply within 30 days. Within 48 hours where life or liberty is concerned.
help.rights.4: A first appeal within 30 days of the decision, or of the date the reply was due. No fee.
help.rights.5: A second appeal or complaint to the Central Information Commission, which is a separate body.
help.writing.title: Writing a request that gets answered
help.writing.1: Ask for records, not opinions. An officer must hand over what exists; they need not write you an essay.
help.writing.2: Name the period. “Between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026”, not “recently”.
help.writing.3: Number your points. One question per number gets one answer per number.
help.writing.4: Do not ask why a decision was taken. Ask for the file notings that show how it was taken.
help.scope.title: What cannot be filed here
help.scope.body: This portal reaches Central Government public authorities only. Land records, ration cards, police stations, driving licences, electricity, municipal services, State schools and district hospitals belong to State authorities. A Central portal cannot obtain them, whatever you pay. Use your State's own RTI portal or State Information Commission.
help.refused.title: If you are refused
help.refused.body: Sections 8 and 9 of the Act list the grounds on which information may be withheld. A refusal must cite one. If it does not, or if you think it has been misapplied, that is exactly what a first appeal is for — and it is free.
help.accessibility.title: Accessibility
help.accessibility.body: This prototype targets WCAG 2.1 AA and the GIGW 3.0 design guidance. Text size and high contrast can be changed from the bar at the top of every page, and the setting follows you across the site without JavaScript. Every step works with scripting switched off, on a keyboard alone, and with a screen reader. Nothing here is an image of text.
help.accessibility.report: Found something that does not work for you? In a real service this line would carry a named officer and a response time. In a prototype it is an admission that this is where that commitment belongs.
help.contact.title: Getting a human
help.contact.body: There is no help desk behind this prototype and no telephone number to call, because there is nobody to answer it. The live portal's desk runs 9:00 to 17:30, Monday to Friday, and currently warns of high call volume.
hp.alreadyNote: Sign in to track a request, see its deadline, or appeal.
hp.h1: File a Right to Information request
hp.lead: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, any citizen of India may ask a Central Government public authority for the records it holds.
hp.ask.title: What do you want to know?
hp.ask.label: What information do you want?
hp.ask.placeholder: e.g. how much MGNREGA wage money is pending in my district
hp.ask.note: Any Indian language. Free. No account.
hp.know.title: Know what you need?
hp.stepsLead: Check whether you need to file at all, work out where it goes, and know what to expect.
hp.how1.title: Check whether it is already published
hp.how1.body: Before you file, see whether the information is already out there. Under section 4 of the Act every public authority has to publish a great deal of its own accord, and past RTI replies are public once they have been released.
hp.how1.body2: Describe what you want and RTI Sahayak looks first. If it is already published you have it in seconds, and you pay nothing.
hp.how2.title: Identify the right public authority
hp.how2.body: Your request has to go to the body that actually holds the records. This portal reaches Central Government public authorities only — 2,581 of them, grouped under 94 ministries and departments.
hp.how2.body2: Land records, ration cards, police stations, electricity, municipal services and State schools belong to State departments, and go to your State's own RTI portal instead. The fee is ₹10, or nil if you are below the poverty line, and you never have to say why you want the information.
hp.how3.title: What happens after you file
hp.how3.body: The Central Public Information Officer has 30 days to reply, or 48 hours where life or liberty is at stake. If another authority holds the records, your request must be transferred to them within 5 days. Some records may be withheld under sections 8 and 9.
hp.how3.body3: No reply within 30 days counts as a refusal. You may then appeal to the First Appellate Authority within 30 days, free of charge. They have 45 days to decide, after which a second appeal goes to the Central Information Commission within 90 days.

ind.note: Illustrative figures, invented for this prototype. The live portal publishes no figures of this kind, which is itself the point: a citizen cannot find out whether requests like theirs get answered.

dir.onlyTitle: These are the only bodies you can file with here
dir.onlyBody: If the records you want are held by a State department, a municipal body, a State police force or anything else not on this list, this service cannot obtain them. Go to that body's own RTI portal and file there. Filing here would cost you the fee and the wait, and the application would come back.
hp.scopeBody: State departments — land records, ration cards, police, electricity, municipal services — cannot be reached from this portal. We tell you before you pay, not after.
faq.q1: Who can file an RTI application?
faq.a1: Any citizen of India. No age limit, no reason required, no lawyer.
faq.a2: ₹10, fixed by the RTI Rules 2012. Nil if you are below the poverty line and provide a certificate. A first appeal is free.
faq.q3: How long does a reply take?
faq.a3: 30 days. 48 hours where life or liberty is concerned. Silence past 30 days counts as a refusal you can appeal.
faq.q4: Can I file against a State department here?
faq.a4: No. This portal covers Central Government public authorities only. State subjects go to your State's own RTI portal or State Information Commission.
faq.q5: Do I have to say why I want the information?
faq.a5: No, and nobody may ask. Section 6(2) of the RTI Act, 2005.
faq.q6: What if I paid and got no registration number?
faq.a6: On the live portal a payment can take 24 to 48 working hours to reconcile, and there is a Payment Reconciliation page for recovering the request. In this prototype the number is issued immediately, because no money moves.
login.lead: This screen is for Nodal Officers, Central Public Information Officers and First Appellate Authorities.
login.notBuilt: Not built in this prototype. There is no officer module here, no account system, and no credentials of any kind — so there is nothing to sign in to and nothing to steal.
login.why: It is in the menu because the live portal puts officer sign-in as the sixth of ten items in the middle of a citizen menu, unlabelled, where citizens click it and get stuck. Naming it, and moving it out of the citizen's path, is the fix.
login.citizen: If you are a citizen, you never need to sign in. Filing, tracking and appealing all work without an account — that is deliberate, and the live portal gets it right too.
contact.lead: There is no help desk behind this prototype, and no telephone number, because there is nobody to answer it. Everything below is what the live service publishes.
contact.liveBody: Published on rtionline.gov.in: a telephone number staffed 09:00 to 17:30, Monday to Friday except public holidays, and an email address. At the time of our audit the page also warned callers of high call volume.
contact.designTitle: Why we have not copied it
contact.designBody: A help desk is the symptom, not the service. Most calls it takes exist because a screen did not say what went wrong. Every error in this prototype names the problem and the next step, in the language you are reading, which is the cheaper fix.
contact.accessBody: In a real service this line would carry a named officer and a response time, as GIGW requires. In a prototype, saying so is an admission of where that commitment belongs.
contact.auditBody: Built for a hackathon from a read-only audit of a public website. Nothing was submitted to the live portal and no account was created there.

ai.title: RTI Sahayak
ai.subtitle: Describe what you want to know, in any Indian language. RTI Sahayak works out who holds it and whether this portal can reach them — before you are asked for any money.
ai.placeholder: Type your question, in any Indian language
ai.onNote: An OpenAI model read your question and suggested where it belongs. Every suggestion is checked against our own authority list before it is shown, and the keyword match below is computed without the model.
ai.offNote: No AI model is configured, so this is deterministic keyword matching. Every match shows which of your own words caused it. The result is the same every time.
ai.disclaimer: AI can be wrong. Nothing is filed and nothing is charged until you have read and approved the application yourself.
ai.verdictCentral: This looks like a Central Government subject
ai.verdictState: This looks like a State subject
ai.verdictUnclear: Not enough to go on yet
ai.error: The AI service did not respond. The keyword match below still works.

arch.whyBody: Once information has been released under the Act it is public. The next person to ask the same question should find the answer, not pay ₹10 and wait thirty days for it again.
wiz.p1: Records about you and about the country are spread across 2,581 Central Government public authorities, and across offices inside them. Most people do not know which one holds what.
wiz.p2: RTI Sahayak reads your question in your own words and works out where it belongs — or tells you it is a State subject this portal cannot reach, before you pay anything.
wiz.p3: It also checks whether the answer is already published, or was released to somebody who asked before you. Quite often it was.
wiz.orAsk: Or describe it in your own words
wiz.q1: How long does a PF withdrawal claim take to settle?
wiz.q2: How much MGNREGA wage money is pending in my district?
wiz.q3: How many post-matric scholarship applications are pending?
wiz.q4: How long does police verification for a passport take?
wiz.q5: How much was refunded for cancelled trains last year?
wiz.q6: How many Ayushman Bharat claims were rejected?
wiz.q7: What is the status of the national highway project near me?
wiz.q8: How many income-tax refunds are pending beyond a year?
auth.login.why1: Every request, appeal and receipt in one list, instead of one lookup screen per task.
auth.login.why2: The statutory clock on each filing, and a warning before the thirty days run out.
auth.login.why3: Your details typed once, not retyped on every form.
auth.login.why4: One appeal button on the request it is about — no registration number to copy across.
auth.login.costBody: An account is a record of who asked what. The live portal has no citizen account, and that is one of the few things it gets right. You can file here without logging in; this exists so your filings have somewhere to live.
auth.login.methodNote: Whichever you filed with. A mobile number works the same as an email address here.
acct.expiry: Drafts, filings and saved details are held for 24 hours in this prototype, then deleted.
acct.dash.lead: Everything you have filed, with the statutory clock on each one.
acct.dash.attentionNone: Nothing is waiting on you. The clock is running on everything below.
acct.dash.countsNote: These six numbers are the whole of the live portal's dashboard. Registered means ever filed, so a returned request is counted there too.
acct.dash.profilePromptBody: The live form asks for your name, address, gender, education and habitation on every single request. Fill them in once here and every request you file is filled in for you.
acct.dash.profileDone: Saved. Your next request will be filled in from these.
acct.dash.reason.replied: A reply has arrived. Read it, and appeal if it is incomplete.
acct.dash.reason.overdue: Thirty days have passed with no reply. That is a deemed refusal, and you can appeal for free.
acct.dash.reason.window: The appeal window is open and closes on {date}.
acct.new.fileBody: One page, ₹10. The checks — already published, right authority, Central subject — run before you pay, not after.
acct.new.fileCta: Start or file a new request
acct.new.searchBody: RTI Sahayak finds what is already published and names the authority that holds the rest.
acct.new.pubBody: If it is out there already, you do not need to file at all.
acct.new.dirBody: The 2,581 bodies this prototype can file with.
acct.new.scopeNote: Land records, ration cards, police and municipal services belong to State authorities — use your State's RTI portal for those.
acct.new.draftTitle: You have a draft in progress
acct.new.draftBody: Not filed. Nothing has been paid.
acct.track.lead: Where each filing is, and how long the public authority has left.
acct.track.none: Nothing is in flight. Anything you file will appear here with its deadline.
acct.track.lookupBody: A registration number is enough on its own. The live portal also demands the email address it was filed with and a captcha, on a screen called Online RTI Status Form, which is also the name of four other screens.
acct.history.lead: Everything filed from this account, newest first.
acct.history.note: On the live portal this list is behind an email address, a mobile number, a captcha and a one-time code, and it keeps three years. Here it is one click, and the prototype keeps 24 hours.
acct.history.caption: Requests and appeals filed from this account
acct.history.none: Nothing filed from this account yet.
acct.appeals.lead: A first appeal goes to the First Appellate Authority inside the same public body. There is no fee — that is statutory, not a concession — and you have thirty days.
acct.appeals.readyNote: Pick the request. Everything the appeal form needs is already on file, so nothing is retyped.
acct.appeals.none: None of your filings can be appealed today.
acct.appeals.noneBody: An appeal becomes possible when a reply arrives, or the day after thirty days pass with no reply.
acct.pay.lead: Every rupee this account has been charged, and what it bought.
acct.pay.caption: Payments made from this account
acct.pay.none: Nothing has been charged to this account.
acct.pay.reconBody: The live portal has a whole menu item for this, called Payment Reconciliation, because money can leave your account without a request being created. In this prototype nothing can be lost, because no money moves: the fee is a mocked step and the registration number is written in the same instant.
acct.pay.bplNote: Below the poverty line? The fee is nil, with proof. Set it in your account information and the fee step disappears.
acct.profile.lead: The live request form asks for all of this on every single filing, and remembers none of it. Fill it in once and every request and appeal you make here is filled in for you.
acct.profile.saved: Saved. Your next request will be filled in from these.
acct.profile.name: Full name
acct.profile.emailHint: Where the reply and every alert is sent.
acct.profile.mobileHint: For SMS alerts. Optional on the live request form and mandatory on its history screen, which is how people lock themselves out of their own filings.
acct.profile.stateHint: Where you live — not the government your request goes to.
acct.profile.habitationHint: The live form labels this Status, with the options Rural and Urban and no explanation.
acct.profile.educationHint: Asked by the live form. It changes nothing about your request or your rights.
acct.profile.citizenshipHint: Only Indian citizens may file an RTI request — section 3 of the Act.
acct.profile.citizenshipWarn: Section 3 of the RTI Act gives the right to information to citizens of India. A request filed on this basis will be returned.
acct.profile.bpl: Are you below the poverty line?
acct.profile.bplHint: If yes, there is no fee at all — section 7(5). Proof is attached to the request itself.
acct.profile.bplWarn: Demonstration fields. Do not type a real card number: nothing here is transmitted anywhere, and it is held in the same 24-hour store as everything else.
acct.profile.noIds: What this form does not ask for
acct.profile.noIdsBody: No Aadhaar number, no PAN, no card details and no password. None of them is needed to ask a question of your government, and none of them is collected here.
acct.profile.useItBody: Your name, email, address and PIN code are placed in the request form for you. Every one of them stays editable at the moment of filing.
compose.fromProfile: Filled in from your account information. Change anything that has moved.
pay.nilBody: Your account information says you are below the poverty line. Section 7(5) of the Act sets the fee at nil, and the live portal asks for proof as an attachment to the request. There is no payment step for you.
file.intro: One page: choose the authority, say what you want to know, check your details. The ₹10 fee comes at the end, after every check has run.
file.fromSahayak: RTI Sahayak has filled in what it learned from your conversation. Change any of it — nothing here is decided for you.
file.suggestedNote: RTI Sahayak suggests this body from your words — change it if you know better.
file.askInstead: Not sure who holds it? Ask RTI Sahayak first.
file.qLabel: Search and tell us your issue — what do you want to know?
file.qHint: In your own words, in any Indian language. Before you pay, we check whether this is already published and whether this portal can even carry it.
file.errQuestion: Please say what you want to know.
file.draftLetter: Start the letter for me from my words above
file.forcePay: I am sure this is Central — continue anyway
file.publishedLead: Before you pay: this looks already published
file.publishedGo: None of these — continue to payment
file.beforePay: Nothing is charged yet. The next page confirms the ₹10 before anything happens.
file.signInNote: No account needed. Log in and these details are saved once, filled into every request after this one.
file.detailsLead: The live form asks for all of this on every request and every appeal, and remembers none of it. Fill it in once and it is saved to your account.
file.detailsOnce: This question is asked once. Never again.
file.doneLead: Keep the registration number — it is the only handle on your request.
file.doneNote: The CPIO must reply within {days} days — by {date}. The reply and every alert go to the email address you gave.
pay.aboutTo: The fee is {fee}, fixed by the RTI Rules 2012. It is not refunded if the application is later returned — so check the summary below before you continue.
pd.s1.title: Find it before you file it. File once. In your own language.
pd.s1.sub: A working re-imagining of rtionline.gov.in, organised around the three problems citizens actually hit.
pd.s1.note: Unofficial prototype · not a government service · built by Puneet Vishnawat
pd.s2.title: Where a citizen's time goes before anything is answered.
pd.s2.c1.d: Nothing published is searchable, so citizens file all over again.
pd.s2.c2.d: Every form re-asks the last one; every status needs a number from an email.
pd.s2.c3.d: Two languages, an unsortable list, and a form that accepts invalid requests.
pd.s3.title: If the answer is public, the request should never be filed.
pd.s3.problem: Much of what citizens ask is already published — it simply cannot be found, so it is asked again and answered again.
pd.s3.c1.d: An AI chatbot searches published information, documents and released RTI replies in plain language.
pd.s3.c2.d: Every processed RTI made browsable — fewer duplicate requests, more transparency.
pd.s3.outcome: Fewer duplicate RTIs — answers in minutes, not 30 days.
pd.s4.title: Verified once. Remembered always. Everything one glance away.
pd.s4.problem: Name, address, contact and BPL status are re-entered on every filing; tracking means pasting a number from an email.
pd.s4.c1.d: Verifies who you are, your BPL status and your details in one step — the form fills itself in.
pd.s4.c2.d: Your details are saved, and every later filing reads from them.
pd.s4.c3.d: Track all your RTIs, deadlines and appeals from your profile.
pd.s4.c4.d: External requests are still trackable by number.
pd.s4.note: Aadhaar verification is part of the plan, not yet built — the prototype's sign-in is a mock code that verifies nothing.
pd.s5.title: Built for the one person the portal exists for.
pd.s5.c1.d: The full Eighth Schedule, each named in its own script — today the portal offers two.
pd.s5.c2.d: 2,916 bodies that filter as you type, each labelled Central or State.
pd.s5.c3.d: Rule-based checks stop invalid requests before they are filed.
pd.s5.c4.d: Simpler structure on any phone, on slow connections, with the journey working with JavaScript off.
pd.s5.note: Eleven of the 22 languages are translated in the working prototype.
pd.s6.title: Built with Codex. Powered by OpenAI.
pd.s6.1: The assistant calls an OpenAI model server-side only — the key never reaches the browser.
pd.s6.2: Codex ran three adversarial review passes; a statutory bug, an open redirect and an authorisation gap did not survive them.
pd.s6.3: Next.js server actions on Cloudflare Workers at the edge; KV drafts; no database, no origin.
pd.s7.title: Every claim carries a check that fails when it stops being true.
pd.s7.1.n: WCAG 2.1 AA, both themes, read from the stylesheet.
pd.s7.3.n: The full journey with scripting disabled.
pd.s8.title: Real and mocked, separated on screen.
pd.s8.real.1: The journey, routing and statutory clock
pd.s8.real.2: Search, the published-answers log and the profile
pd.s8.real.3: 22 languages named in the switcher, 11 translated
pd.s8.mock.2: The sign-in code — any six digits
pd.s8.note: Nothing was ever submitted to the live portal. No government logos. The banner on every page cannot be dismissed.
pd.s9.title: Three fixes. No new law required.
pd.s9.sub: Make published answers findable. Verify once and remember. Speak every language of the Eighth Schedule. The fee, the timelines and the Act stay exactly as they are.
